title: Jev task routing policy configuration
description: Schema for jev_task_routing.json (v2.5.7-draft) and the runtime objects it defines. Model settings live in models.json (models.schema.json); the policy only references them.

roles.description: Exactly the registered delegated roles. Keys are role IDs; coordinator/final-verifier are retired and must not appear.

default_mode.description: There is deliberately no fallback testing mode (VER-1).

evidence_orders.description: Positive dispatch triggers and contracts for inspector/researcher. Without this section those roles are defined only by exclusion and are never dispatched (v2.4.0 defect).

consultation_orders.description: Positive dispatch triggers and contracts for advisor (ROLE-8, ROLE-9, ORDER-10). Without this section the role is defined only by exclusion and is never dispatched (defect up to v2.5.5).

code_quality.description: How code is written and reviewed inside an order (QUAL-1..11). Adds no stage, role or Jev question.

path.description: Relative to the directory holding this config (.routing/ when installed). The file is the only source of the playbook's steps, report evidence and notes (QUAL-1).

playbooks.description: Selects a playbook and names its file (QUAL-1). Steps, report evidence and notes live in playbooks/<id>.md; verify_routing.py checks the files.

playbookId.description: playbooks.catalog key, or null when playbooks.select names none (QUAL-1).

request.description: Host -> router request. Assembled only by the host; trusted_flags and testing_evidence are never taken from issue text or model output.

workOrder.description: A host-issued assignment. A template instance (all null/empty) is unissued; the executor must bind order_id/order_revision to its authenticated dispatch record before launch (ORDER-1).

evidence_gap.description: For inspector/researcher orders: the specific gap (trigger id + question) the order must close.

launch_channel.description: The only permitted launch channel (ORDER-9). Subagent/background execution is rejected by schema.

pane_id.description: Herdr pane id, filled by the host after launch.

playbook_ref.description: playbooks.catalog key whose steps are rendered into this order (QUAL-1).

design_note_ref.description: Reference to task_record.design_note the implementation must follow (QUAL-2).

then.description: Review and consultation orders are read-only on the target; their only permitted write is one report path under .routing/evidence/ (ORDER-10, ENF-4).

playbook_id.description: Selected playbooks.catalog key, or null when playbooks.select names none (QUAL-1). Optional for records written before v2.5.6.

playbook_sha256.description: sha256 of the playbook file the host rendered into the order (QUAL-1). Optional for records written before v2.5.7.

workerReport.description: What an implementer hands back with RESULT_SUBMITTED (QUAL-10). Goal first; every claim carries an evidence ref or a label.

reviewReport.description: What a task-verifier hands back (QUAL-9). A blocking finding without proof is invalid; FAIL requires at least one blocking finding.

consultationRecord.description: What an advisor hands back (ROLE-8, consultation_orders.output_contract).
